messages:
Sara Liu: heads up — been poking at routing policy bugs in canary, seeing a bunch of accidental tenant-wide fallthroughs. thinking of a small linter to catch common footguns.
Tom Chen: nice. can you sketch what rules you want?
Sara Liu: basic ideas: 1) require explicit match for tenant_id or tenant_tag when route scope != global; 2) warn on overlapping path matches with different quotas; 3) deny configs that set quota > project limit without a slack approval tag.
Jia Patel: also add: warn if there is a fallback route that points to a lower-tier model without an explicit SLO annotation. that one caused surprises last week.
Matt Rogers: +1. telemetry team needs structured annotations so console can show which routes are eligible for fallback autopromote. if linter enforces annotation shape, dashboards get better signals.
Leah: can we make linter pluggable and run it in CI and the Console config editor? want quick feedback before deploy.
Tom Chen: yes — plan: build rule set as YAML, implement a small CLI that outputs code-style diagnostics and a machine JSON output for the Console.
Sara Liu: sample rule snippet I imagined:

```yaml
- id: require-tenant-scope
  severity: error
  description: "Routes that are not global must include tenant selectors"
  match: route.scope != 'global'
  condition: route.selectors.tenant != null
```

Matt Rogers: that looks good. include a quickfix suggestion when severity=warning so Console can offer "Add tenant selector" button.
Jia Patel: question: how do we handle protobuf vs json route manifests? Engineering ops mostly checks YAML in repo, but runtime uses protobuf blobs. linter should validate both representations.
Tom Chen: we can run linter against the repo YAML and also wire it into the runtime validation step that receives proto. reuse rules by canonicalizing proto -> json via proto reflection.
Sara Liu: exact — canonicalizer will be small. we should also check for quotas that mismatch tenant billing plan, e.g., heavy quota on free-tier.
Leah: rollout UX: feature flag the linter enforcement. step 1: warnings in CI and Console; step 2: require warnings resolved for canary; step 3: enforce as errors for prod.
Ryan (infra-bot): deploy-bot: new lint-ruleset v1 uploaded to s3://redwood-lint/routing/v1 at 2024-06-12T15:20Z.
Tom Chen: what about false positives for legacy configs? need an allowlist per repo.
Jia Patel: allowlist yes, but prefer an opt-out annotation on route with `lint:skip_reason` with limited TTL. prevents permanent technical debt.
Sara Liu: agree on TTL. also we should add a telemetry tag when linter auto-fixes something (manual quickfix via Console) so we can track resolution rate.
Matt Rogers: telemetry events we want: lint.warning_emitted, lint.error_emitted, lint.auto_fix_applied, lint.allowlist_used. include route_id, repo, author, and canary_flag. keep payload small.
Tom Chen: console needs a list API: GET /lint/results?route_id=xyz returning array of diagnostics. use protobuf for the wire format but JSON for browser UI.
Jia Patel: can we add a dashboard widget that surfaces "Top Lint Violations by Team" and "Potential Quota Risk"? that will help product owners prioritize fixes.
Leah: rollouts: when enforcing as errors, we should gate by service-level quota budget. don't want linter enforcement to block urgent rollbacks. propose an enforcement whitelist for emergencies.
Sara Liu: emergency whitelist + audit log. any bypass must create a ticket and auto-expire.
Ryan (infra-bot): reminder: any new lint rule that triggers >100 warnings org-wide will be flagged for slow-roll.
Tom Chen: implementation plan: week1: rule DSL + CLI + CI hook. week2: Console integration + quickfix UI + telemetry events. week3: proto canonicalizer + runtime validation hook. week4: slow-roll enforcement on staging.
Matt Rogers: can I own Console quickfix UI? I can mock up wireframes today.
Leah: I'll add feature flag config and rollout plan to the release doc.
Jia Patel: I'll draft the telemetry schema and update the evals so fallback SLO annotations get surfaced.
Sara Liu: thanks team. last thing — let's include a tiny example of a bad config to catch:

```yaml
routes:
  - id: r1
    path: /generate
    scope: team
    model: gpt-3-embed
    quota: 2_000_000 # looks high, no tenant selector -> should error
```

Tom Chen: ok that triggers require-tenant-scope + quota-risk rules.
Ryan (infra-bot): note: created ticket PLAT-4823 for lint-ruleset and assigned to Sara.
Sara Liu: will start a draft PR for CLI today. ping me in #eng-platform if you want review. :rocket:
Matt Rogers: ack, will wire console mock tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Leah: adding rollout checklist to the release doc now.
Jia Patel: thanks all, will sync telemetry with Matt after mock is up.
Sara Liu: and we'll iterate rules over the slow-roll period — start conservative and add stricter ones once noise is down.
